I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks (`tsc --strict`), and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 2287 bytes (min+gzip) with 85 bytes of own code. I couldn't compare results against the original, because lodash isn't installed. I checked behaviour against lodash's documented semantics and ran the es-toolkit functions on your example inputs.

I didn't follow the skill's guidance. It says every function is identical to lodash and that compat should never be used. That is wrong here, so I checked each function myself.

| Function | Import | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | `es-toolkit` | Within your input range it matches lodash: arrays merge by index, new keys are deep-cloned, and the target is mutated and returned. |
| `startCase` | `es-toolkit/compat` | The main version lowercases the rest of each word, so "ABC def" gives "Abc Def". Lodash gives "ABC Def", and your input range includes consecutive capitals. |
| `isEmpty` | `es-toolkit/compat` | The main entry point has no `isEmpty`. The compat version returns `true` for numbers and booleans, as lodash does. |

Importing everything from compat would be larger: 3749 bytes against 2287. So I used the main `merge` and compat only for the other two.

The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged, and there are no hand-written replacements or other source files.
